claim_reviews.reason: The amount, three-year period and comparison with 2026 match the operative draft and current law. Statements about economic adequacy and the desirability of more relief are opinions, not additional factual conclusions.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The draft grants €5.525 billion annually for three years, nearly €1 billion below 2026.

evidence_checks.check: Proposed §24d(1) physical page 3; EnWG §24c(1). €0.975 billion is reasonably described as nearly one billion.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Retain unresolved. Cross-country and fossil-energy price comparisons need a use case, energy-service efficiency, tax treatment and price period. Higher ct/kWh alone would not determine heat-pump, combustion or industrial-process economics.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Electricity remains expensive internationally and relative to fossil energy.

evidence_checks.check: ZVEI physical page 1; Eurostat and Monopolkommission comparative methods checked. No exact fossil alternative, household or industrial cohort is identified by the author.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Unresolved is appropriately conservative for the multi-group up-to-25% claim. A household model alone cannot verify the same upper share for commerce and smaller industrial users, whose profiles, tax treatment and contracts differ. The phrase can also be an illustrative scale rather than a literal universal cap.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Network charges account for up to25%of prices for household, business and smaller industrial users.

evidence_checks.check: ZVEI original physical page 1; BDEW household model is not the full required commercial/industrial cohort. No error inferred without resolving the intended population and upper-bound reading.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported mechanism and documented variation. Voltage level, distributed generation, upstream withdrawals and tariff structure jointly affect the subsidy cascade. Actual effects for each 2027 company or region have not been predicted.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Subsidy effects differ substantially with network level and region.

evidence_checks.check: Consentec section 4.1 and direct 2026 tariff sheet comparisons; StromNEV cost cascade. ZVEI itself cites the commissioned study but legal and operator evidence are independently checked.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported as planned reform for 2029. Consultation status and the scheduled expiry of the old ordinance are relevant; no final implementation claim is made here.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: AgNes is a planned tariff-system reform for the transition to 2029.

evidence_checks.check: Official BNetzA 6 August announcement, full draft and StromNEV expiry provision. Original ZVEI page 2 calls it an announced reform during the transition.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported by current law and the draft. Preserve the author’s 18 August date, while actual dispatch and receipt are unverified; the stated consultation window does not prove late delivery.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The proposal reduces annual subsidy from €6.5 billion in 2026to €5.525 billionfrom 2027.

evidence_checks.check: EnWG §24c(1), proposed §24d(1); thyssenkrupp original physical page 1. No inference about the company’s actual submission event.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Keep unresolved for the unnamed political all-inclusive objective. The actual government industrial-price programme uses a wholesale-price benchmark and subsidises only a defined consumption share, but the author is partly articulating its own broader policy target. That ambiguity is not a factual error.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: A politically formulated industrial-electricity goal is €50/MWh inclusive of network charges and all state price components.

evidence_checks.check: Pre-author BMWE releases dated 16 April and 26 May: 5 ct/kWh wholesale basis, 50% of eligible consumption. No identified political statement establishes the stronger all-inclusive objective with this exact scope.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Retain unresolved under the conservative protocol, with the modal nature preserved. Individual tariffs can plausibly dampen effects, but a zero-benefit case depends on physical-path costs, upstream-node treatment, reserve costs, floors and contracts. No specific facility outcome was verified.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Individual network tariffs can reduce or eliminate the subsidy benefit for some industrial users.

evidence_checks.check: StromNEV §19(2), Consentec, and independently checked BNetzA physical-path position paper/FAQ from initial allocation. The original says can be less or absent in an individual case; it does not report a measured zero benefit for thyssenkrupp.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: The verified legal content is the one-off non-payment safeguard. In context, the company’s mention of revocation is a concern about security, not an explicit assertion that ministers have unlimited budget discretion. Do not silently broaden the law or manufacture an error from that policy wording.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The draft permits a within-year tariff adjustment if subsidy payment fails.

evidence_checks.check: Draft §24d(6), physical page 4; six-week notice and shared TSO decision; supplier and investment-security commentary on original page 2. The draft condition is non-payment/legal impossibility.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Unresolved recipient-specific time limit is correct. The stated general ministry window does not authenticate when this author received its invitation or draft, and its complaint of inadequate time is partly normative.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The consultation period available to the counties was only about one week.

evidence_checks.check: Original dated 12 August, physical page 1; protocol ministry interval 5–13 August. No recipient invitation record or individual delivery evidence recovered.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: The draft term, annual amount and KTF financing match. A claim that this is the best long-term financing choice would be normative and has not been treated as a fact.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The draft pays €5.525 billion/year for three years from KTF.

evidence_checks.check: Proposed §24d(1) and full draft rationale; original Landkreistag physical page 1. Current law gives the distinct 2026 comparator.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported in the direct accounting sense. Financing recognised costs through a grant reduces the tariff funding requirement but does not itself lower the physical cost of the grid. Indirect behavioural effects are outside this bounded proposition.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The subsidy changes who finances network costs rather than directly reducing system costs.

evidence_checks.check: Draft cost rationale and §24d(5) deduction from revenue caps. Original page 1 says financing shifts to the federal budget; it does not claim total long-run behavioural effects are identically zero.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Both calculations are exact at the stated precision. The numbers compare annual subsidies rather than total network costs or individual retail prices.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: The subsidy falls by €975 million or15%compared with 2026.

evidence_checks.check: €6.5 − €5.525 = €0.975 billion; €0.975 / €6.5 = 15%. Draft and current law independently compared.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported qualitative description of cost categories and congestion mechanisms. It does not allocate a quantified share to any cause or prove that every proposed integrated plan would reduce them.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Transmission costs include expansion/capital costs and congestion-management/redispatch components.

evidence_checks.check: StromNEV recognised cost base, regulatory accounts and Monitoringbericht investment/redispatch information; AgNes rationale on network and congestion-management costs.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: The original explicitly requires temporal coordination and control. Under that condition, local balancing and flexibility can relieve upstream withdrawals or expansion requirements. Annual energy balance alone is insufficient, and it is not a verified saving for a named region.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Coordinating local generation, demand, storage and sector coupling can reduce upstream grid use and expansion needs.

evidence_checks.check: Landkreistag physical pages 2–3 re-read; Consentec vertical-flow mechanism; BNetzA AgNes and cost-efficiency rationale. Spatial, temporal and technical constraints preserved.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Supported with an important limit: regulation recognises a calculated return and cost recovery subject to eligibility and efficiency rules, rather than guaranteeing realized profit. This narrower legal premise is explicit in the original wording of recognised equity return.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Regulated network operation allows recognised returns on equity and regulated revenue recovery.

evidence_checks.check: StromNEV §§4–7; proposed TSO framework capital and revenue provisions. Costs and returns can be reviewed, so underperformance or disallowed assets remain business risks.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

claim_reviews.reason: Retain unresolved for the comparative magnitude of municipal project risks. The listed development, finance and marketing risks are plausible, but a general claim that they are materially greater than regulated network risks needs a defined project set and comparison. The fairness judgement is separately normative.
claim_reviews.reviewed_claim_en: Regional municipal energy projects face substantial development, financing and marketing risks relative to regulated networks.

evidence_checks.check: Original Landkreistag physical page 2; regulatory return framework checked, no comparative municipal-project risk dataset recovered. No contradiction inferred from missing comparative evidence.
evidence_checks.independent_result: No error established; see review reason for outcome and limits.

omissions.original_excerpt: Auch diese Maßnahme kommt nicht den Verbraucher:innen, sondern nur der Industrie
omissions.claim_en: The industrial electricity-price programme directly benefits eligible industrial companies rather than ordinary households.
omissions.reason: C014 inventories the budget numbers but not this separate eligibility premise. The pre-author BMWE programme release identifies energy- and trade-intensive industrial sectors as direct beneficiaries. Read as direct programme eligibility, this is supported; do not infer there can be no indirect effect on households through product prices or employment.

evidence_checks.locator: Official BMWE releases dated 16 April and 26 May 2026, direct eligibility and consumption limits
Independent primary search result for 16 April BMWE release

omissions.merge_option: May be appended to C014 with a separate supported eligibility subclaim while its exact budget figures remain temporally unresolved.

omissions.original_excerpt: Steigende Stromkosten können die Investitionsentscheidungen von Haushalten
omissions.claim_en: Other relevant conditions held fixed, higher electricity operating costs can make investment in electric technologies less attractive.
omissions.reason: This is a material conditional premise behind retaining the larger subsidy, distinct from the flexibility mechanism in C043. Higher input costs reduce a project’s operating-cost advantage with capital costs, efficiency, expected use and other prices fixed. Primary policy analysis recognizes this substitution incentive. It does not verify any actual number of foregone heat pumps, vehicles or industrial conversions, or prove a higher subsidy is optimal.

evidence_checks.locator: Printed page 340, paragraph 807, lower electricity costs make electricity more attractive for substitution
COM(2026)600 explanatory memorandum, coordinated taxation and tariff incentives for electrification

omissions.scope_limit: Conditional relative operating-cost mechanism; actual adoption effects and magnitudes remain unmeasured.

limitations: All eight original documents and all 22 physical pages re-read; 60 of 60 claims reviewed. Reading repeated for peer review adds zero new reading units.
No error candidate is proposed. Two temporal downgrades and two evidence-locator corrections are research-record revisions, not allegations against authors.
Exact published draft identity with the original individual dispatch and actual delivery dates remain unverified; later corroboration is explicitly distinguished from author-date evidence.
Full raw underlying 25-operator market-check data were not available; the reported sample average was checked for attribution, methods, unit and consistency rather than independently re-estimated.

Some frozen source anchors are too short to identify their proposition on their own, such as C001 “einen der”, C020 “sofortigen”, C053 “lediglich einer” and C058 “zeitlicher”. They are exact but should be expanded to informative contiguous original phrases in the synthesized report. The frozen raw inventory has not been edited.

Public source downloads can return a challenge despite HTTP 200. The attempted BMWE original HTML was explicitly marked unusable; labelled primary web extraction was used instead. A guessed January BDEW PDF URL returned 404 and supplies no evidence.
No author contact, human specialist review, facility-specific tariff reconstruction or causal estimate of investment uptake was undertaken.
